newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Fator-led group to advise Brazil state power sale.
newsitem.headline: Fator-led group to advise Brazil state power sale.

text.p: The southern Brazilian state of Rio Grande do Sul said a consortium led by local investment bank Banco Fator will advise the state on the restructuring of its power sector.

The group is comprised of Banco Fator, Fator Projetos e Assessoria, Fator Corretora de Valores e Cambio, Kleinwort Benson Ltd, Kleinwort Benson do Brasil, Deutsche Bank SA, Morgan Grenfell & Co, Jaakko Poyry Engenharia Ltda and Azevedo Sodre Advogados, a state spokeswoman said.
The consortium will help the state implement its model for the reshaping of the power sector and draw up a privatization plan for the state's power distribution and coal firms.

Under the model, the state will transfer its thermoelectric power generators to the federal government and privatize coal firm Companhia Riograndense de Mineracao and two electricity distributors, she said.

"We plan to release tender documents for the sale of the first power distributor in July. We hope to release bid specifications for the sale of the second distributor in September," the spokeswoman said.
The two distributors account for 64.6 percent of the state's electricity sales, she said.
The state will keep its hydroelectric plants, wholesale power distribution company CEEE and an electricity distributor serving the state's south region, she added.
Energy consumption in Rio Grande do Sul reached 3,000 megawatt hours (MWh) last year. The state generates 1,000 MWh and buys the rest from federal power firm Eletrobras' Eletrosul unit.
